name: Kaike
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Regmi, Ambika. 2013. A Grammar of Magar Kaike (LINCOM), not online; read Honda 2008 (Nepalese Linguistics 23, Digital Himalaya PDF) - no stress statement for Kaike

new_statements.quote: The analysis of the suprasegmental system of Kaike is still under way. In the 10th Himalayan Linguistics Symposium held in Thimphu, Bhutan, I presented a preliminary analysis on the sound system of Kaike (Honda 2004) and reported that Kaike is a tonal language. However, the tonal analysis presented at that time and also in the 12th HLS, in 2006, was revised, and the revised analysis should be discussed in detail somewhere else. In this paper, therefore, no suprasegmental feature will be described, yet, for the sake of comparison with Tamangic languages, it should be mentioned that the Kaike tone system is not the same as the modern Tamangic tone system [...] (p. 92)
new_statements.citation: Honda, Isao. 2008. Some observations on the relationship between Kaike and Tamangic. Nepalese Linguistics 23: 83-115.
new_statements.locator: p. 92 (section 2, sound system; PDF p. 10 of the extracted article) and pp. 109-110 (conclusion)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kaike is described as a tonal language; no source opened gives any rule for word stress. Honda 2008 explicitly declines to describe any suprasegmental feature; Regmi & Regmi 2016 (p. 72, by the author of the LINCOM grammar) add only 'Bhujel is an atonal language whereas Magar Kaike is a tonal language. Both lack contrast in length.'
new_statements.exceptions: None; Honda notes only that the Kaike tone system differs from both the modern Tamangic two-manner/four-tone system and Mazaudon's old Tamangic three-manner/two-tone system.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone is implied (lexical items compared with Tamangic); no statement about word vs phrase domain or citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Kaike of Sahartara/Tupatara/Tarakot (and Belawa) villages, Sahartara VDC, Dolpa district; autonym 'Magar Kaike' (Regmi), 'Kaike' (Honda). No dialect split is reported; same variety as Glottolog kaik1246 (alt. name Tarali Kham).
